correctness.rationale: Bisections up to complement are in bijection with C(19,9)=92378 masks containing vertex zero, so complete 30-edge cut enumeration is exhaustive; cubicity makes boundary cost even. Independent Python enumerated all 92,378 and obtained histogram {6:10,8:330,10:2232,12:10560,14:22680,16:27330,18:18760,20:8166,22:2190,24:120}. Independent graph-distance BFS verified exactly ten complement-distinct radius-two ball masks and equality with all minima. Enumerating every selected/unselected pair swap generates cost<=8 adjacency: 340 vertices, 2520 edges, full 340-root BFS confirms connected, eccentricity histogram {5:280,6:60}, radius five and diameter six. Every minimum pair has either four common cost-eight neighbors (15 pairs) or none (30 pairs); graph of fourfold pairs is 3-regular on ten, strongly regular parameters (10,3,0,1) and diameter two, identifying Petersen. Minimum pairs have 2 or 4 swap distances, and evenness plus no min-min edge proves budget slack two is minimal. All checks are COMPLETE finite enumeration, not a random experiment or larger graph inference.
residual_risks: The exhaustive finite graph code should be retained for future external replay; it is not a general theorem of all dodecahedral-like graphs.

value.rationale: The first cost slack needed to move between all global balanced-cut optima is a natural optimization sensitivity invariant. Its smallest possible value two is forced by parity and the complete graph at that level is 340-state connected with a nontrivial Petersen bridge structure and fourfold transition multiplicity, reusable in reconfiguration and bisection benchmark studies. The finite graph is canonical rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
residual_risks: Only one twenty-vertex graph, no uniform fullerene reconfiguration theorem.
